title: Hobbycast Episode 8 (NEW UPLOAD): Video Podcast - Asian Cinema Nostalgia - Part 3
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gK1VHYEXt_0

Part three widens the net beyond Hong Kong. Daniel (@dungeondive) flips through Thai action from the *Ong-Bak* stunt crew, Takashi Miike's *Full Metal Yakuza* and *Fudoh*, and a run of Korean titles where *Sympathy for Lady Vengeance* has overtaken *Oldboy* for him on rewatch. A Bollywood science-fiction epic, a live-action *Devilman* that lost the anime's excess, and Tsai Ming-liang's *Goodbye, Dragon Inn*, which he calls a Chinese *Last Picture Show*, all pass through.

Then the pile turns back to old-school kung fu and stays there. Daniel explains the three broad styles of classic choreography, wuxia swordplay, chaotic open-hand brawling, and the staccato "shapes" films built to show off perfect form, using *Monkey Kung Fu* as the example. The new Shaw Brothers Blu-rays get a look: *Legendary Weapons of China* with its voodoo-doll sorcery and the Gordon Liu versus Lau Kar-leung duel, *Heroes of the East* with its marital dispute settled by a parade of Japanese masters, and King Hu's *Come Drink with Me*. *Seven Grand Masters* is named as having the best fight scenes he has ever seen. There is a lament about restorations so clean the wires show, a warning about bootleg imprints selling twenty discs for ten dollars, and a note that *Born Invincible* sits complete on YouTube.

----

Daniel says the Celestial restorations are almost too good, because now you can see the wires. Does cleaner always mean better for older genre films?
